predecessors.name: Chera Perumal kingdom
predecessors.text: North Malabar from the Chandragiri river (Kasaragod) to the Korappuzha, between the Arabian Sea and the Kodagu/Wayanad hills

successors.name: East India Company
successors.text: North Malabar from the Chandragiri river (Kasaragod) to the Korappuzha, between the Arabian Sea and the Kodagu/Wayanad hills

ledger.x: c.1100: the Kolathiri kingdom (Kolathunadu) of North Malabar, from Chandragiri river to Korappuzha, successor of the Mushika/Ezhimala line, as the Chera Perumal realm ends.
1792: Malabar formally ceded to the British; Chirakkal, Kottayam and Kadathanad Rajas acknowledge Company sovereignty.
1792: Kolathunadu absorbed into British Malabar; last Kolathiri Raja died 1801.

certainty.note: Traditional river bounds only; real control fragmented among Kolathiri branches, Arakkal, Nileshwaram and Kadathanad, and Mysore held Malabar 1766-1790.
